Hi Emma / Raj —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a short list of clarifying questions so we can scope the architecture review:  

1) Primary requirement: Hospix wants customer-identifiable PII to remain in the EU region for processing and primary storage. Please confirm whether that applies to all environments (prod, staging) or only prod.
2) Backups / DR: you indicated you can tolerate backups replicated to the US for disaster recovery if encryption + strict access controls are applied. Can you confirm maximum allowed retention for cross-region backups (days)?
3) Failover behavior: need to confirm whether automatic cross-region failover is acceptable or if you prefer manual failover with documented approval. Also capture RTO/RPO targets if you have them.
4) Logging / audit: confirm whether you need raw request logs preserved (token-level logs) or a hashed/redacted audit trail is sufficient.

Attached: PII-data-flow-diagram.pdf (diagram of suggested flow) and Redwood-Residency-FAQ.pdf (short FAQ & options matrix).

Next steps I propose: once you confirm answers above we’ll get Mina (solutions engineer) to prepare a short architecture note with RPO/RTO options and a recommended pinning + backup policy. Would you like a 30-45m technical call next week or a written proposal first?

Thanks — I’ll push the doc into the HubSpot deal record after we hear back.

Thanks Jonas — good writeup. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency scope: EU-only for prod workloads. Staging and dev can be global but must not contain live PII.
- Cross-region backups: acceptable to store encrypted backups in the US for DR, provided backups are encrypted with customer-controlled keys and access is restricted to a named subset of Redwood engineers. Retention: maximum 30 days for cross-region backups; primary EU copies can be longer if needed.
- Failover: prefer manual failover to start; automatic failover requires a formal DR runbook and approval from our security/ops team.
- RTO/RPO: our goal is RTO <= 4 hours, RPO <= 1 hour for production. If you have options that offer shorter RTO/RPO with cost tradeoffs, list them.
- Logging: we do not want full raw request logs containing PII preserved outside the EU. A hashed/audit-only view is preferred. We will request sample retention and a redaction policy for review.

Please loop in Mina for the technical options and thanks for the attachments.

Emma Liu
Head of Data Compliance
Hospix Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>

Hi Emma / team — thanks for the clear constraints. Below are concrete, technical options that map to your requirements and proposed tradeoffs. I’ve kept the language practical and included the default Redwood behavior vs optional configurations.

1) Residency / Pinning options
- Hard pin (EU-only): primary compute, primary storage, and request logs are pinned to an EU region. No automatic cross-region replication of primary data. This meets the strictest residency requirements.
- Soft pin with controlled DR: primary remains in EU, but backups (encrypted) can replicate to a configured DR region (e.g., US-east) — replication is only enabled by account setting and requires an explicit contract amendment.

Recommended for Hospix: Hard pin for primary processing + soft pin for encrypted DR backups with 30-day max retention in the US (per your input).

2) Backups, replication, and RPO/RTO
- Hot replication (nearline streaming): cross-region replication with near-real-time copies. Typical RPO ~ 5–15 minutes, RTO targets depend on deployment: Hosted API (multi-tenant) best-effort recovery ~ 1–4 hours; Dedicated pools (reserved GPUs) can target RTO <= 1 hour with pre-warmed capacity.
- Snapshot-based backups: daily snapshots replicated cross-region. Typical RPO = 24 hours, RTO = 4–12 hours depending on restore workflow.

Tradeoffs: Hot replication reduces RPO but increases egress and storage costs. We can provide both options; you can choose hot for critical buckets and daily snapshot for less-critical data.

3) Logging and audit controls
- Request logging: default Redwood hosted behavior retains request metadata and token-level logs for 90 days. For PII-sensitive customers we offer:
  * Token redaction at ingest (recommended) — removes raw token content before any logs leave the EU.
  * Hashed/audit-only logs — store cryptographic hashes of request IDs and metadata only.
  * Configurable retention windows (7, 30, 90 days)
- Audit trail: full access logs (who/when) can be kept in EU only and exported to your storage via secure transfer.

4) Encryption and key management
- All data at rest and in transit is encrypted. Options: Redwood-managed keys (default) or BYOK (customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM). BYOK + regional key stores can ensure cross-region backups are encrypted under keys that the customer controls, preventing Redwood staff from decrypting without authorization.

5) Access controls and personnel separation
- Cross-region backups: access limited by role-based permissions and bound to named engineers for emergency restores. We can include explicit escrowed approval flows for restores.
- Third-party audits / evidence: we can provide SOC 2 reports, DPA text, and a short technical note mapping controls to your compliance checklist.

Attachments: PII-data-flow-diagram.pdf (annotated), Redwood-Residency-FAQ.pdf (contains matrix of pinning + DR options). I’ve also dropped a short drive folder with sample runbooks and a template DR approval form — link in the thread metadata.

Next steps I propose:
- Jonas/Emma: pick 2x 45-minute slots for an architecture deep-dive where I’ll present the hot-replication vs snapshot restores, show estimated costs for each RPO/RTO profile, and capture required contract amendments (DR consent).
- I’ll prepare an architecture note (1–2 pages) summarizing hard-pin + hot-replica plan and a cost delta.

If helpful: example configurations we can bring to the call:
- Option A (cost-optimized): EU primary + daily snapshot to US (RPO 24h, RTO ~6h)
- Option B (balanced): EU primary + hourly replication to EU backup (intra-EU) with US cold backups (RPO 1h, RTO 2–4h)
- Option C (fast failover): EU primary + hot replication to EU secondary (RPO < 15m) + US cold backups (RTO < 1h with pre-warm)

Happy to provide sample SLAs for Dedicated if you expect stricter RTO targets.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Inference Platform
